newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Mar 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Mar 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- The ashes of the late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping were scattered in the sea by his family.

-- The chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, Li Ruihuan, urged people to treasure the stability they were enjoying. He said by following the theories of Deng Xiaoping, China would have a great future.

-- MING PAO -- The property market in Hong Kong went up again after the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, with 60 apartments of a new development in Discovery Bay being sold out within a morning.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The governor of the People's Bank of China said recently that the central bank's control over credit limits of commercial banks would be loosened this year. Big enterprises would be allowed to issue bonds to raise money.
-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Chinese military leaders complained about a lack of funds and requested the National People's Congress increase the military budget.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- The head of China's Ministry of Public Security, Tao Siju, said whether Chinese security staff carried weapons when attending Hong Kong's handover ceremony would be decided according to international practice.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST-- China looks set to launch its long-awaited family car, called Lucky Star, within 12 months, but without the much-expected heavy involvement of the world's leading care manufacturers.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- China's military chiefs, including Generals Liu Huaqing and Zhang Zhen, closed ranks behind Persident Jiang Zemin, saying they were following the will of Deng Xiaoping.

-- China's National People's Congress was expected to give the Provisional Legislative Council its final legal seal next week by adopting a work report on the formation of the post-transfer government.
